blurb: Discussion: Why India Needs a Politics of Democratic Resistance Are street protests unconstitutional, or are they an essential part of a functioning democracy? This discussion examines the role of popular mobilisation in holding institutions accountable, with the Jantar Mantar protests as a key example. The student protests, which led the government to respond to their demands, were directed towards formal institutions of parliamentary democracy and did not seek to undermine the constitutional order. In an era when several avenues of democratic accountability and responsiveness appear increasingly constrained, street mobilisation can provide an important means for citizens to express their will. The discussion will feature Yogendra Yadav, founding member of Swaraj Abhiyan and Jai Kisan Andolan. A political scientist and noted psephologist, Yadav has been associated with the 2020-21 farmers' agitation, anti-CAA protests and Bharat Jodo Yatra. He was also a Senior Fellow at CSDS, Delhi, and was associated with Lokniti surveys. Note: The above text has been sourced from the event's organisers.

blurb: Wim Wenders' Wings of Desire (1987), originally titled Der Himmel über Berlin, is a poetic romantic fantasy about loneliness, human connection and the beauty of ordinary existence. Set in divided Berlin, the film follows invisible, immortal angels who observe the city and listen to the private thoughts of its inhabitants. Though surrounded by millions of people, many of those they encounter are isolated, troubled or estranged from those they love. One of the angels, played by Bruno Ganz, becomes fascinated by a lonely trapeze artist, portrayed by Solveig Dommartin. His growing desire to experience the world as a human being leads him to make an extraordinary choice: he gives up immortality so he can experience the physical and emotional pleasures of mortal life. Food, touch, colour, pain and love suddenly acquire new meaning. Wenders creates a contemplative film that transforms everyday experiences into moments of wonder. The screening will be followed by a discussion, offering audiences an opportunity to explore the film's ideas and imagery. All are welcome, and entry is free and open to all. blurb: What does migration mean to a woman who leaves behind everything familiar and attempts to build a new life? How much courage, resilience and self-confidence are needed to find one's place in an unfamiliar environment? Nenekkadi Danni, written by Prakashamma, explores these questions through the extraordinary life of her mother, Inyasamma. Rather than presenting migration as an abstract social phenomenon, the book brings the experience alive through Inyasamma's own words, memories and reflections. Her story raises questions about adapting to new ways of life, protecting family and community, negotiating unfamiliar circumstances and finding an individual identity amid changing social realities. The discussion offers an opportunity to engage with the personal dimensions of migration, particularly the experiences of women whose stories are often overlooked in larger conversations about movement and displacement. Participants can meet the world of Inyasamma through her memories and join a conversation around the book, its themes and the many meanings of home, belonging, family and survival. blurb: Can degrowth work in developing countries? Join Let's Debate Degrowth, an engaging discussion exploring one of today's most debated economic ideas. Participants will examine whether reducing consumption and economic expansion can promote sustainability without compromising development goals. The session will distinguish between economy-wide degrowth and sector-specific transitions while considering practical realities faced by emerging economies. Bringing together diverse perspectives, the debate encourages thoughtful dialogue on climate change, resource use, social equity and alternative development models. Whether you're a student, researcher or simply curious about sustainable futures, the discussion promises stimulating conversations and fresh insights.
